title: Find in Mountain Array
summary: A MountainArray object exposes get(index) and length().

contractDetails.constraints: 3–10000 mountain values, each in [0,1000000000]. target is in the same range. The fixture mountainArr array configures the supplied object and is not a directly readable learner parameter.
contractDetails.output-checking: Construct a supplied MountainArray from the fixture. Invoke findInMountainArray(target,mountainArr). get uses zero-based indices and rejects more than 100 calls. Do not pass the raw fixture array to the learner function.

statement: A MountainArray object exposes get(index) and length(). Its values rise strictly to one interior peak and then fall strictly. Return the smallest zero-based index containing target, or −1 when absent. Read values only through get, with at most 100 get calls per invocation.

examples.explanation: The left occurrence precedes the right occurrence.

constraints: 3–10000 mountain values, each in [0,1000000000]. target is in the same range. The fixture mountainArr array configures the supplied object and is not a directly readable learner parameter.
hints: Conceptual: The target may occur on both sides, so the smaller index matters.
Directional: Locate the peak, then search each monotone side.
Implementation: Use adjacent middle values to binary-search the peak. Search the increasing side first, followed by the decreasing side only if necessary.
complexityAnalysis: O(log n) time and get calls, O(1) auxiliary search state. The wrapper enforces the 100-call budget.
